newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Lone Star says gold find may be bigger.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Lone Star says gold find may be bigger.

text.p: Lone Star Exploration NL said it was likely it would lift the resource estimate of its Awak Mas gold prospect in Indonesia above a stated 2.733 million ounces.
In a statement late on Tuesday, Lone Star said the Awak Mas resource had increased 33 percent since its last estimate in January to 2.733 million ounces, grading 0.7 grams a tonne.
"The success of the latest 30,000-metre drilling programme continues to strenghten our belief that Awak Mas is a significant Indonesian gold resource," Lone Star said.
Lone Star holds a 45 percent interest in Awak Mas, a 363 square km patch located on Sulawesi Island.
Gasgoyne Gold Mines NL also holds 45 percent, with the remaining 10 percent held by PT Asminco Bara Utama of Indonesia.

Lone Star said it was able to include a resource of 3.075 million ounces of gold grading 0.5 grams/t in its latest resource as a result of recent mine design and cost studies indicating a lower cut may be appropriate.
Results from Awak Mas continue to exceed the expectations of the partners, Lone Star said.
Because only 75 percent of the gold in soil anomaly has been systematically drilled so far, Lone Star said it expects the resource figure to be further increased.
Drilling is to continue with a view to extending the mineralisation boundaries to the west and north, Lone Star said.
Lone Star is also listed on the Vancouver Stock Exchange under the symbol.
